get.description: 200 whether or not the visitor is signed in, so the UI can ask without a 401 appearing in the console.

post.description: Validate a token WITHOUT storing it; tells the UI which teams, networks and existing apps are visible.

put.description: Where outage alerts go (any https endpoint that accepts a JSON POST). Stored encrypted: Slack-style addresses are secrets.

get.description: CPU and memory of the running app, read from Liara (read-only).
How many releases of the app Liara allows a day and how many were made in the last 24 hours, and the things the agent cannot do through Liara's API.

post.description: What a fix from the diagnosis would do, as the same approval card the assistant shows. Nothing is changed.
Make the change after the person approved its card. The same code path as the assistant's approved card.

get.description: What the agent found by itself the last time the uptime check saw the app go down (nothing when it never did).

post.description: Ask the language model to read the app's evidence (the log tail and what was measured, scrubbed) and propose causes: a second opinion below the rules.

get.description: Why the running app is failing or slow: the signals read now and the likely causes, most likely first, each with what points to it and the fix that follows.
The theme, plugin and language files that would be sent (and the uploads folder if asked). Nothing leaves the server.

post.description: Starts sending the files over FTPS with the access the person made in the Liara console. The password is used for this transfer and not stored.

get.description:
Starts GitHub's authorization. mode=signin: sign in or create an account (asks only for who you are; a server with an invite code needs `invite` for a NEW account).
mode=connect (needs a session): also asks for the `repo` permission, so private repositories can be downloaded and fixes sent as pull requests. Off unless the server has an OAuth app.
GitHub sends the person back here (a browser visit, so every outcome is a redirect). The state must match the signed cookie from the start of this round trip.
Liara's ready-made apps (a snapshot). Those with a spec can be installed here; the rest need a cloud server.

post.description: A project with no source: its plan comes from a ready-made app's spec. Nothing is created on Liara until the run is approved.

A preview deployment: the same repository at another branch becomes its own project, so its app, databases and cleanup are separate
from the main one's. The access token of a private repository is reused, never returned.

delete.description:
Deletes the project, ALL its runs and everything those runs created on Liara (apps, databases, disks, domains...). The project's name must be given as `confirm`.
If Liara cannot be cleaned (an error, or no saved token), nothing local is deleted either, so it can be tried again and nothing is left running unseen.

get.description: Server-sent events. Reconnect with the Last-Event-ID header (or ?after=) to continue without gaps.

post.description:
Stop a run midway. It ends as cancelled at its next step; anything it already created stays (delete it from the run page), and a release already
building on Liara finishes there.

get.description: The run as a Markdown document (names only, no values), as a download.

post.description: A plain-language reading of the run's log from the language model (scrubbed first; no tools, no secrets).

get.description: What the person does at the place the domain is registered (IRNIC's panel for a .ir domain), per domain of the app, with Liara's own nameservers and records filled in.

post.description: What connecting the domain would do. Reads only; nothing is created.
'Check records': asks Liara to look again, and nudges the nameserver check of a pending Liara DNS zone.

get.description: Asks the zone's own nameservers and the big public resolvers about each record of the domain. Reads DNS only; nothing is changed.
The DNS records Liara added for this domain to a Liara DNS zone, which removing the domain can clean up too. Reads only.
Releases of newer code made by this server (newest first): their state while they build, and how they ended.

post.description: Release the newest code of the project's repository on the app this agent already runs (same settings, nothing new created).

A token for the developer's own coding agent. Shown once; only its digest is kept. By default it can read this person's projects and runs and send code fixes; with can_deploy it can also start deployments and answer for the person.

put.description: Who fixes a code error in this project without asking each time: "sakoo", "own_agent", or null (ask).

post.description: The run is waiting for the developer's own agent: stop waiting, Sakoo fixes the code itself.

get.description: What the agent changed in the code to make it run, as a patch: apply it to the repository with `git apply`.

post.description: Opens a pull request on the person's repository with the agent's fixes, on a new branch. Needs a token that can write (the one given for a private repo, or a new one).

get.description: The app's releases on Liara, newest first, with whether each can be rolled back to.

post.description: Make an earlier release the running one again. Creates a new release (Liara builds nothing for a kept source it already knows, but it does deploy).
Like POST /api/chat/messages, but the answer arrives live as server-sent events (step, delta, tool, card, then done).

get.description: The numbers behind the upload/Git error messages, so the UI can show them before the user hits them.

AiHypothesis.title: AiHypothesis
AiHypothesis.description: A second opinion from the language model when no rule explained the problem: below the rules, never acted on by itself.

AppLimitsOut.title: AppLimitsOut
AppLimitsOut.description: What Liara's API limits for this project's app, and what the agent cannot do because the API has no call for it.

ChatActionOut.title: ChatActionOut
ChatActionOut.description: A change the assistant proposed: it runs only when the person approves this card.

DeploysOut.title: DeploysOut
DeploysOut.description: Releases of newer code made by this server, newest first.

DnsCheckOut.title: DnsCheckOut
DnsCheckOut.description:
What the zone's own nameservers and the big public resolvers say about a domain's records. `verdict`: all_good | propagating | missing |
wrong_value | not_at_liara | no_nameservers | unknown.

DomainRecordOut.title: DomainRecordOut
DomainRecordOut.description: A DNS record Liara asks for. `purpose` is the key it was found under in Liara's answer (the API does not document it).

LatestDiagnosisOut.title: LatestDiagnosisOut
LatestDiagnosisOut.description: The diagnosis made automatically when the uptime check saw the app go down (null when it never did).

MetricsOut.title: MetricsOut
MetricsOut.description: CPU and memory of the running app, as Liara reports them (units are not documented, so none is promised).

PrPreviewOut.title: PrPreviewOut
PrPreviewOut.description: What a pull request would contain. Nothing is sent to GitHub by the preview.

RemovalPlanOut.title: RemovalPlanOut
RemovalPlanOut.description: What removing a domain could also clean up in the developer's Liara DNS zone.

SessionOut.title: SessionOut
SessionOut.description: Never an error: lets the UI ask "am I signed in?" without a 401 in the console.

UptimeOut.title: UptimeOut
UptimeOut.description: The last 24 hours of checks. `up_percent` and `current` are null until the first check.

WpPlanOut.title: WpPlanOut
WpPlanOut.description: What would be sent to the managed WordPress site over FTPS. Nothing is sent by the preview.
